Overview - Magnetic Grids for Sieves
The last check under the screen
A sieve removes oversize material. It does not remove iron of the same size as the product, and a worn screen sheds its own wire. A magnetic grid under the screen catches both.

The grid is a frame of magnetic rods sized to sit in the sieve outlet or the hopper mouth. Product falls between the rods and iron holds to them. Lifting the grid out and wiping the rods takes a minute.

We stock round grids of 10, 12, 15 and 24 inch and 350 mm, and square grids of 6, 8 and 12 inch. Other sizes and shapes are made to drawing. Used on flour, sugar, spices, plastics, chemicals and pigments.

Overview - Neodymium Magnetic Rod
The part every separator is built from

Each rod is a sealed stainless tube holding neodymium magnets and steel pole pieces, machined and welded at our works. Rods are supplied singly, built into grids with side plates, or fitted into an existing filter housing.

Standard rods are 7,000 to 8,000 gauss. High strength rods go to 9,000, super high strength to 11,000 and extreme high strength to 13,500 gauss. Ferrite and Ferrearth rods are made for coarse iron at lower cost.
The tube is watertight, so rods work in liquid lines as well as dry product. Rare earth rods should stay below 100 degrees Celsius. Every rod comes with a tested certificate of magnetic strength.

Overview - Magnetic Sampling Probe
A quick answer on contamination
Push the probe into the material and draw it out. Any iron in the batch is now on the sleeve. Slide the magnet core out of the sleeve and the iron drops onto a tray for inspection or weighing.
Used as a routine check on incoming material, and as a fast way to find which stage of a line is shedding metal. A clean probe after the final separator is useful evidence for an auditor.
T-handled magnetic probe with a sliding sleeve for checking sacks, bins and hoppers for iron. 304 stainless steel, neodymium core.

Overview - Magnetic Separation Grids
Simple protection on a gravity line
Product falls through the grid. Every path between the rods passes within a few millimetres of a magnet face, so nails, wire, swarf and fine iron hold to the rods while the product carries on.
A one stage grid has a single row of rods. A two stage grid has two rows, offset, so nothing can fall straight through. Two stage grids are used where the particles are fine or the flow is fast.
Grids are lifted out for cleaning and wiped by hand. They are used at intake hoppers, above mixers and mills, and at bagging points in food, plastics, chemicals and minerals.

Overview - Underflow Magnetic Separator
The first magnet in the line
The plate sits in the chute floor so the product slides straight over the magnet face. Large iron pulls down onto the plate and stays there until the plate is swung clear and wiped.
Fitted before grids and rod separators, it takes out the large pieces that would otherwise bridge across the finer rods or damage them. Made to the chute width and burden depth.
